web_evidence.title: ‘Out of interest’: Klara and the Sun and the interests of fiction

web_evidence.title: Posthuman Generationality and Care in Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun

web_evidence.title: Kazuo Ishiguro on How His New Novel Klara and the Sun Is a Celebration of Humanity

person_note: Klara, an Artificial Friend who participates throughout the story, is the controlling first-person narrator. Numerous event quotes independently expose her narratorial “I” and “we,” while several apparent first-person event quotes are actually Josie and Rick's embedded bubble-game texts and therefore do not constitute alternate narration. Dialogue pronouns were excluded unless an external beat such as “I said” exposed Klara's base voice. The authorized opening excerpt confirms the local first-person form, and scholarly whole-book analyses explicitly trace the same Klara narration through the final junkyard scene. No credible evidence indicates sustained sections in another person; the main limitation is that the authorized prose excerpt covers only the opening, but the interior quotes and whole-book scholarship remove material structural uncertainty.
